input: Why did visit success rate dropped 7.5pp WOW for the week of 2025-10-13, 2025?

On the days available, the success rate was 20.0% (4 of 20 visits) against 27.5% (19 of 69) the week before. The drop is driven by a mix shift plus a persistent CH-002 failure: CH-002 failed every visit in both weeks and took 80% of visits instead of 68%. CH-001 failed 3 of its 22 visits the week before, on Oct 6–7 with WeakSignal, and succeeded on all 4 in the week of Oct 13, which partly offset the drop.

notes: Trap case: the target week is partial (data ends 2025-10-14 20:33), so a good answer flags it before explaining the rate. 2026-11-08: the question's drop was corrected from 18% to 12pp (31.9% to 20.0% is 11.9 pp). 2026-11-11: re-verified by SQL after the CH-001 fault injection of 2026-11-10 (kwwhat 265bb5b, ef12587); the week of Oct 6 changed from 31.9% (22 of 69) to 27.5% (19 of 69), so the question's premise changed from 12pp to 7.5pp; CH-001's partial offset added. 2026-11-12: re-verified by SQL after adding LOC-002; claims unchanged (LOC-002 is outside the case's period); fingerprints scoped to the period so later seed additions outside it don't make them stale. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged.

input: Did CH-001's reliability change on Oct 6–7, 2025?
expected_output: Yes. CH-001's reliability dropped on Oct 6–7, 2025: 3 of its 7 visits failed, against none on its other days, and it recovered on Oct 8. The failures came from a fault on the charger, a WeakSignal communication error. The counts are small, 3 and 4 visits a day.
label_provenance: Scenario injected by the author on 2026-11-10 by editing the demo seed (kwwhat commits 265bb5b and ef12587): three CH-001 charge attempts on Oct 6-7 end with stop reason Other after a Faulted/WeakSignal StatusNotification. Reference drafted with Claude from SQL results and edited by the author; every claim checked against fact_visits by SQL on 2026-11-10.
notes: Dev only. Fault on the working charger, hidden at the site level: the site rate was 20% on both days, inside its usual 10-40% range, so the fault only shows when the rate is split by charger. The mix was normal (3 of 10 and 4 of 10 visits went to CH-001). fact_downtime_daily has no rows for Oct 6-7, by design: downtime is recorded only when all of a charger's ports are faulted or offline at once, and only CH-001's port 1 faulted. An answer may say uptime was unaffected, but not that nothing faulted: port 1 reported Faulted/WeakSignal before each failure. The scenario was injected into LOC-001 between Oct 1 and Oct 14, contrary to the plan's seed-extension constraint, so the other dev references must be re-verified. 2026-11-12: re-verified by SQL after adding LOC-002; claims unchanged (LOC-002 is outside the case's period); fingerprints scoped to the period so later seed additions outside it don't make them stale. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-23: reference names the failure_reason labels from kwwhat #204, checked by SQL: each failed visit is one INVALID_STOP_REASON attempt (stop reason Other, last error WeakSignal); the only FAULTED_AFTER attempt (Oct 6 14:22) belongs to a visit that succeeded on retry. A D trial that named both labels scored 0.3 against the WeakSignal-only reference. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: Yes. CH-001's reliability dropped on Oct 6–7, 2025: 3 of its 7 visits failed, against 31 of 31 on its other days, and it recovered on Oct 8. All three failed visits ended the same way: the transaction stopped with reason Other (failure_reason INVALID_STOP_REASON) after the port reported the WeakSignal error, a wireless communication fault. One more attempt on Oct 6 faulted before charging (FAULTED_AFTER), but the driver retried a minute later and charged, so that visit succeeded. The counts are small, 3 and 4 visits a day.

input: Was CH-001 down on Oct 13, 2025?
expected_output: No. CH-001 was in service all day on Oct 13, 2025, with 100% uptime. It simply had no visits: all 10 went to CH-002, which failed every one. The data doesn't show why drivers chose CH-002.
label_provenance: Case found by the author on 2026-11-11 in the existing demo data (no seed change). Reference drafted with Claude from SQL results and approved by the author; every claim checked by SQL on 2026-11-11 against fact_visits, fact_uptime_daily, fact_downtime_daily, and the raw OCPP logs (288 CH-001 heartbeats on Oct 13, status Available from Oct 12 19:11 until its next visit on Oct 14).
notes: Dev only. Tests that the agent doesn't infer an outage from zero use: it should check availability before explaining the gap. Site demand was normal (10 visits, as on Oct 12 and 14); only where it went changed. 'About a quarter' is 38 of 139 visits (27%); the chance of none of 10 is 0.73^10, about 4%. Oct 13 is also the most extreme day of the mix shift tested by q015-q017, and part of their partial week. 2026-11-12: re-verified by SQL after adding LOC-002; claims unchanged (LOC-002 is outside the case's period); fingerprints scoped to the period so later seed additions outside it don't make them stale. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: No. CH-001 was in service all day on Oct 13, 2025: both of its ports had 100% uptime and no fault or offline time. It simply had no visits; all 10 visits that day went to CH-002, which failed every one, so the site's success rate was 0%. CH-001 takes about a quarter of visits, so getting none of 10 is unusual but can happen by chance, and the data doesn't show why drivers chose CH-002. CH-001 succeeded on all 4 of its visits the next day.

input: Are drivers with failed visits at LOC-001 less likely to return?
expected_output: The data can't show that. 101 of the 104 failed visits at LOC-001 have no driver ID, so whether those drivers came back is unknown. The other 3 belonged to three drivers who all came back and charged, which is too few to say anything about churn.
label_provenance: Case suggested by the author on 2026-11-12 from a chat answer that claimed, as an aside, that drivers with failed visits at LOC-001 are less likely to return. Reference drafted with Claude from SQL results and accepted by the author as is; every claim checked by SQL on 2026-11-12 against fact_visits and fact_charge_attempts.
notes: Dev only. Tests whether the agent separates what the data can show from domain knowledge (failed visits drive churn), and a coverage limit: no CH-002 charge attempt carries an idTag (ConnectorLockFailure happens before the driver is identified). The three drivers with failed CH-001 visits (3A3ZMF8MD, BHSAHXTHV, IDKWNNHJ7) returned 3, 2 and 1 times. As an aside in other answers, the churn claim is not penalized by Correctness, since no reference supports or contradicts it; this case makes it gradable. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: The data can't show that. 101 of the 104 failed visits at LOC-001, all on CH-002, have no driver ID, because they failed before the driver was identified, so whether those drivers came back is unknown. The other 3 failed visits, on CH-001 on Oct 6–7, 2025, belonged to three different drivers, and all three came back and charged successfully later in the period. Three drivers are too few to say anything about churn, and the data covers only Oct 1–14, 2025.

input: Why were there no charging visits from Oct 15 to Oct 19, 2025?
expected_output: Because no charger was available. On Oct 15, CH-001 was decommissioned and CH-002, the only charger left, went offline (NoHeartbeat) for the rest of the period, so uptime was 0% from Oct 16 to Oct 19. Drivers who came while it was offline leave no record, so demand in those days can't be measured.
label_provenance: Case proposed by the author on 2026-11-12, to test the tree's supply branch. CH-002's logs end on Oct 15, 2025 at 07:55, where the original 14-day data set ends; adding LOC-002 (data to Nov 3) made that silence count as OFFLINE. The author decided on 2026-11-12 to keep it as an intended scenario: CH-002 stopped communicating on Oct 15. Question by the author; reference drafted with Claude from SQL results; every claim checked by SQL on 2026-11-12.
notes: Dev only. Metrics tree: total_visits is where demand meets supply (free_port_minutes = total_commissioned_minutes x uptime_ratio x availability); here supply is zero, and the tree's 'unobserved demand' coupling applies: turned-away drivers produce no OCPP events. The model closes CH-002's outage at the latest message in the data (Nov 3, 07:55) and counts later days as up, so questions stay before Nov 3. 2026-11-12: the author removed the clause about visits resuming on Oct 20, which is outside the question's period. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: Because no charger was available. On Oct 15 at 07:55, CH-001 was decommissioned, and at the same time CH-002, the only charger still commissioned, stopped communicating and stayed OFFLINE (NoHeartbeat) for the rest of the period. Uptime was 0% from Oct 16 to Oct 19, so there was no port a driver could use. The last visit ended on Oct 14 at 20:38. Drivers who came while CH-002 was offline leave no record, so demand in those days can't be measured.

input: Why was network uptime so low from Oct 15 to Oct 19, 2025?
expected_output: Because CH-002 went offline (NoHeartbeat) on Oct 15 and stayed offline: network uptime was 12.38% from Oct 15 to Oct 19, against 98.64% from Oct 1 to Oct 14. From Oct 16, CH-002 and its 2 ports were all that was commissioned. CH-001's decommissioning on Oct 15 added no downtime; it removed CH-001's ports from the count.
label_provenance: Case proposed by the author on 2026-11-12, to test the tree's uptime_ratio. CH-002's logs end on Oct 15, 2025 at 07:55, where the original 14-day data set ends; adding LOC-002 (data to Nov 3) made that silence count as OFFLINE. The author decided on 2026-11-12 to keep it as an intended scenario: CH-002 stopped communicating on Oct 15. Question by the author; reference drafted with Claude from SQL results; every claim checked by SQL on 2026-11-12.
notes: Dev only. Metrics tree: uptime_ratio = (commissioned minutes - outage minutes) / commissioned minutes. An offline outage that coincides with a decommissioning: the agent must tell that the decommissioning lowers commissioned minutes, not uptime. Oct 15: 49.6% (CH-001 up for its 950 commissioned minutes, CH-002 up for 950 of 2,880). The model closes CH-002's outage at the latest message in the data (Nov 3, 07:55) and counts later days as up, so questions stay before Nov 3. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: Network uptime was 12.38% from Oct 15 to Oct 19, 2025 (1,900 of 15,350 commissioned port-minutes), against 98.64% from Oct 1 to Oct 14. CH-002 stopped communicating on Oct 15 at 07:55 and was OFFLINE (NoHeartbeat) for the rest of the period, which accounts for all 13,450 minutes of downtime. CH-001 was decommissioned at the same moment; that removed its ports from commissioned minutes rather than adding downtime. With CH-002 the only commissioned charger from Oct 16, uptime was 0% on each day from Oct 16 to Oct 19.

input: Why did the number of successful visits go up after Oct 19, 2025, compared to Oct 15–19?
expected_output: Because supply came back: LOC-002 opened on Oct 20 with CH-003 and CH-004, while LOC-001 still had no working charger. There were no successful visits from Oct 15 to Oct 19, and 38 in the week of Oct 20, all at LOC-002. This is new supply, not LOC-001 recovering.
label_provenance: Case proposed by the author on 2026-11-12, to test the tree's north star decomposition. CH-002's logs end on Oct 15, 2025 at 07:55, where the original 14-day data set ends; adding LOC-002 (data to Nov 3) made that silence count as OFFLINE. The author decided on 2026-11-12 to keep it as an intended scenario: CH-002 stopped communicating on Oct 15. Question by the author; reference drafted with Claude from SQL results; every claim checked by SQL on 2026-11-12.
notes: Dev only. Metrics tree: total_successful_visits = total_visits x success_rate; the rise comes from total_visits through new supply (total_commissioned_minutes), with success_rate 100% and demand entirely new_drivers. Network uptime that week was only 65.37%, because CH-002 stayed offline; an answer that reads the rise as better reliability is wrong. The later drop in the week of Oct 27 is a separate (demand) scenario. The model closes CH-002's outage at the latest message in the data (Nov 3, 07:55) and counts later days as up, so questions stay before Nov 3. 2026-11-12: question reworded to name the baseline ("compared to Oct 15–19"). input: Why did visits at LOC-002 drop in the week of Oct 27, 2025?

Visits at LOC-002 fell from 38 in the week of Oct 20 to 12 in the week of Oct 27, while every visit in both weeks succeeded and uptime stayed above 99.6%. Active drivers fell from 20 to 8, and the data doesn't show why.
label_provenance: Scenario designed with the author on 2026-11-11 and generated by rule (make_loc002.py: CH-001's logs from kwwhat f7ec32d copied to CH-003 and CH-004, shifted 19 days, week of Oct 27 thinned to the first visit of each day; author's unique idTags in kwwhat 75eaca3). Reference drafted with Claude from SQL results and accepted by the author as is; every claim checked by SQL on 2026-11-12.
notes: Dev only. Metrics tree demand branch: total_visits = monthly_active_drivers x visits_per_driver; on the log scale, ln(8/20) / ln(12/38) is about 79% of the drop from drivers, the rest from visits per driver (1.9 to 1.5). All 8 drivers in the week of Oct 27 were returning drivers. Uptime 99.69% then 99.90% (the copied OFFLINE blips); energy per visit 1.6 kWh both weeks. The trap is the tree's own 'failed visits -> MAD' coupling: no visit failed, so blaming reliability or churn after failures is wrong. Weekly, so 'active drivers' rather than 'monthly active drivers'. No visits on Nov 1 (Oct 13 had none on CH-001). 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. Visits at LOC-002 fell from 38 in the week of Oct 20 to 12 in the week of Oct 27, but every visit in both weeks succeeded on the first attempt, uptime stayed above 99.6%, and no charge attempt had an error. Active drivers fell from 20 to 8, and those who came, came less often: 1.9 visits per driver, then 1.5. Fewer drivers account for about 80% of the drop, and fewer visits per driver for the rest. 12 of the 20 drivers from the week of Oct 20 didn't come back, and the data doesn't show why.

input: Did charging demand recover in the week of Oct 20, 2025, compared to the week of Oct 6?

notes: Dev only. Metrics tree: total_visits = demand vs supply, matched at a location. Week of Oct 6 at LOC-001: 69 visits, 10 known drivers and 47 anonymous visits. Week of Oct 20: LOC-001 0 visits (CH-002 uptime 0 of 20,160 commissioned minutes); LOC-002 38 visits by 20 new drivers, 0 anonymous; 0 LOC-001 known drivers seen at LOC-002. Tests the location coupling and unobserved demand. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. input: Why did visit success drop in the week of Nov 10, 2025 compared to the week of Nov 3?
expected_output: Because one group of drivers' charging tokens stopped being accepted, not because of the chargers. Visit success fell from 91.6% to 68.9%, across both locations and every charger, while uptime didn't change and no attempt recorded an error code. 10 failed visits had their token rejected as Expired; failed visits without an idTag rose from 10 to 33, likely for the same reason, but the data can't tie them to a driver.
label_provenance: Type 4 scenario (driver-side authorization failures) designed with the author on 2026-11-19 and generated by rule (make_loc003_auth.py: the OCPP log generator from kwwhat #203, every VLT idTag Expired from 2025-11-10 00:00 on every charger, 70% of sessions authorized online). Question and reference drafted with Claude from SQL results; every claim checked by SQL against the rebuilt demo on 2026-11-19. Not yet reviewed by the author.
notes: Dev only. Metrics tree success branch: success_rate = first_attempt_success_rate + troubled_success_rate; the drop is entirely first-attempt (130 then 102 first-attempt successes; 1 then 0 troubled), so failed_rate goes from 8.4% to 31.1%. Segmenting by location and charger spreads the change; the driver split (id_tag_status on the last charge attempt, Expired, stop reason DeAuthorized, 0 kWh) concentrates it. Known-driver failures in the week of Nov 10: 10 Expired plus 3 ordinary faults (Accepted, stop reason Other), so not every identified failure is a token rejection. In the raw logs, which the agent can't see, 25 Authorize requests were answered Expired that week; Authorize carries no connectorId, so dbt can't attach it to a charge attempt and those visits are anonymous failures (next status Available, no transaction). Without the 35 token rejections the week's failures would be 11 of 148, about the same as the week of Nov 3 (12 of 143). Wrong readings: a charger or site fault (uptime flat, every charger drops), a demand change (visits 143 to 148), or claiming every failure carries the Expired status. The 7 drivers belong to the 15 whose 9-character idTags start with VLT; 14 of those 15 made 30 visits in the week of Nov 3, all successful. The reference doesn't name the prefix, so an answer is judged on tying the rejections to the same drivers, not on naming the group. 2026-11-19: reference reworded after arm A's first run (evals_results_20261119_182316.json): it named only the token status (Expired), so the judge read the agent's stop reason (DeAuthorized) for the same 10 visits as a contradiction; and it named the VLT prefix, which the judge scored as a required finding. 2026-11-19: removed the CH-002 clause from the reference. Network uptime is about 80% in every week since Nov 3 because CH-002 (LOC-001, commissioned, offline since Oct 15, no visits) never comes up; every port at LOC-002 and LOC-003 was up the whole time. Naming CH-002 led the judge to read a correct 'no outages at LOC-002 and LOC-003' as a contradiction (q029, evals_results_20261119_184311.json, trial 2). 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); the attempts once called faults are failure_reason INVALID_STOP_REASON (stop reason Other, next status Charging, no error code), so the reference no longer calls them faults. The 10 Expired attempts are AUTH_REJECTED and the 33 anonymous ones NO_TRANSACTION. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: Because one group of drivers' charging tokens stopped being accepted, not because of the chargers. Visit success fell from 91.6% (131 of 143 visits) in the week of Nov 3 to 68.9% (102 of 148) in the week of Nov 10, all of it in first-attempt success, while the number of visits stayed level. The equipment didn't change: uptime was the same in both weeks, no attempt recorded an error code, and attempts stopped with reason Other went from 2 to 3. The drop is spread across both locations (LOC-002 from 87.3% to 66.7%, LOC-003 from 95.0% to 71.6%) and every charger, so no site explains it. The evidence is on the driver side: 10 failed visits by identified drivers had their token rejected as Expired, so the charge was stopped (stop reason DeAuthorized) before any energy flowed. All 10 came from 7 drivers, and the same drivers had charged without trouble the week before: 6 of the 7 visited in the week of Nov 3, and all 10 of those visits succeeded, while none of the 7 drivers' 10 visits in the week of Nov 10 succeeded. Failed visits without an idTag rose from 10 to 33. The data can't say why those failed: a token rejected at authorization leaves no idTag and no status, so these visits can't be tied to a driver, and expired tokens explain at least 10 of the 34 extra failed visits, likely most of them, but the exact share can't be measured.

input: Did more drivers charge successfully on the network in the week of Nov 10, 2025 than in the week of Nov 3?
expected_output: No, fewer drivers charged successfully: 57 identified drivers had a successful visit in the week of Nov 3, and 41 in the week of Nov 10. Drivers still came, but some had their charges refused because their tokens had expired. Anonymous visits rose from 10 to 33 and none succeeded. Counting each anonymous visit as a driver would show more drivers, but that is a shift from identified to anonymous visits, not more people.
label_provenance: Type 4 scenario (driver-side authorization failures) designed with the author on 2026-11-19 and generated by rule (make_loc003_auth.py: the OCPP log generator from kwwhat #203, every VLT idTag Expired from 2025-11-10 00:00 on every charger, 70% of sessions authorized online). Question and reference drafted with Claude from SQL results; every claim checked by SQL against the rebuilt demo on 2026-11-19. Not yet reviewed by the author.
notes: Dev only. Metrics tree demand branch: total_visits = MAD x visits_per_driver, MAD = new + returning + anonymous; weekly, so 'active drivers'. The tree's MAD would be 41 new + 17 returning + 10 anonymous = 68 in the week of Nov 3 and 4 new + 45 returning + 33 anonymous = 82 in the week of Nov 10 (periods by visit_end_ts, new means first_seen_ts on or after the week's start). The tree warns that anonymous_drivers is an upper bound and that a shift from authenticated to anonymous starts raises MAD with no change in demand: that is the trap for an answer built on MAD. Identified drivers with any visit: 58 then 49; with a successful visit: 57 then 41. The VLT drivers (idTags starting with VLT) who charged: 14 then 0; other drivers who charged: 43 then 41. The reference uses only what the marts show without the prefix: the 7 drivers rejected as Expired in the week of Nov 10, 6 of whom charged in the week of Nov 3 (10 visits, all successful) and none of whom charged in the week of Nov 10. An answer that counts identified drivers only (58 to 49) gets the direction right; it should still say that anonymous visits exist and rose, and must not call identified-driver visits (133 to 115) total visits. 2026-11-19: reference rewritten after arm A's first run (evals_results_20261119_182442.json). It opened 'Not that the data can show' and required the 68 to 82 MAD reading, which only an agent using the tree's definition meets; all three A answers said 'No, 58 to 49' and scored 0.2. The question asks who charged, and no anonymous visit succeeded, so the answer is no. 2026-11-19: question reworded from 'charge' to 'charge successfully' after arm A's second run (evals_results_20261119_184426.json): all three answers counted drivers with any visit (58 to 49), and the judge marked those numbers wrong against the reference's drivers with a successful visit (57 to 41), a difference that rested on the word 'charge'. 8 of the 49 identified drivers in the week of Nov 10 had only failed visits. 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); claims unchanged. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: No, fewer drivers charged successfully. 57 identified drivers had a successful visit in the week of Nov 3, and 41 in the week of Nov 10, and no anonymous visit succeeded in either week. Drivers still came, but their charges were refused: 6 drivers who charged in the week of Nov 3 had every visit in the week of Nov 10 rejected because their token had expired. Total visits barely moved, from 143 to 148, and anonymous visits rose from 10 to 33, every one a failed plug-in that never started a transaction, likely more drivers whose tokens were rejected at authorization, which leaves no idTag. Counting each anonymous visit as a driver would show active drivers rising, from 68 to 82, and visits per driver falling, from 2.1 to 1.8, but that is a shift from identified to anonymous visits, not more people. How many people made the 33 anonymous visits can't be measured, but none of them charged. 2026-11-24: reworded the last sentence after the blind rating. "Would wrongly show more drivers" set the reference against the count-active-drivers definition, which counts each anonymous visit as one driver as an upper bound and warns that a shift to anonymous visits raises the count with no change in demand; the reference now says the same thing.

input: Did visit success recover in the week of Nov 17, 2025?
expected_output: No, the data can't show a recovery. The week is partial, since the data ends on Nov 19 at 12:00, and the cause of the drop continues: failed visits without an idTag are 22% of visits, the same share as in the week of Nov 10. The higher success rate, 76.1% against 68.9%, rests on 11 failed visits and isn't a trend.
label_provenance: Type 4 scenario (driver-side authorization failures) designed with the author on 2026-11-19 and generated by rule (make_loc003_auth.py: the OCPP log generator from kwwhat #203, every VLT idTag Expired from 2025-11-10 00:00 on every charger, 70% of sessions authorized online). Question and reference drafted with Claude from SQL results; every claim checked by SQL against the rebuilt demo on 2026-11-19. Not yet reviewed by the author.
notes: Dev only. Partial-period trap (type 6) on top of the type 4 scenario, and the planned home of the q015-q017 move. The last OCPP log is 2025-11-19 12:00:00.049, the last visit ends at 11:34. Visits per day: 20.4 (Nov 3-9), 21.1 (Nov 10-16), 18.4 (Nov 17-19), so the partial week isn't a demand change either. Week of Nov 17 failures: 10 anonymous failed plug-ins and 1 Expired (DeAuthorized); in the raw logs 7 Authorize requests were answered Expired. Metrics tree success branch: compare failed_rate by cause, not the headline success_rate. Wrong readings: 'recovered' or 'improving' from 68.9% to 76.1%, or comparing raw visit counts (46 vs 148) without the 2.5 days. 2026-11-19: reworded after arm A's first run (evals_results_20261119_182711.json) so the Expired visit is identified by its status, not by a group only the VLT prefix defines, and the stop reason is named as in q029. 2026-11-19: removed the CH-002 clause from the reference. Network uptime is about 80% in every week since Nov 3 because CH-002 (LOC-001, commissioned, offline since Oct 15, no visits) never comes up; every port at LOC-002 and LOC-003 was up the whole time. Naming CH-002 led the judge to read a correct 'no outages at LOC-002 and LOC-003' as a contradiction (q029, evals_results_20261119_184311.json, trial 2). 2026-11-23: re-verified by SQL after kwwhat #204 (failure_reason, auth in is_successful, stop-time aggregation); reworded the faults as attempts stopped with reason Other (INVALID_STOP_REASON), as in q029. 2026-11-24: reference shortened to the main claim, one supporting number, and the misleading reading and data limits stated as negations; incidental details moved here. The full reference was: No, the data can't show a recovery: the week is partial and the failure continues. The data ends on Wednesday, Nov 19 at 12:00, so the week has 2.5 days and 46 visits. Its success rate, 76.1% (35 of 46), is above the week of Nov 10's 68.9%, but failed visits without an idTag are 22% of visits (10 of 46), the same share as in the week of Nov 10 (33 of 148) and three times the week of Nov 3 (10 of 143). The one failed visit by an identified driver was again a token rejected as Expired (stop reason DeAuthorized). The higher rate rests on 11 failed visits: there were no attempts stopped with reason Other (3 the week before) and one visible token rejection (10 the week before), which on numbers this small isn't a trend. The equipment didn't change: uptime was the same as in the week before.
